rv.q: And thus Sharyn Rothstein’s gutsy “Right to be Forgotten,” which has been very shrewdly cast and honestly staged at the Raven Theatre by the capable young director Sarah Gitenstein, comes as an incisive and sharp-toothed relief.
'Right to Be Forgotten' is unforgettable, and comes highly recommended.
“Right To Be Forgotten” is both of its time and timeless and will have you question your own beliefs about what should and shouldn’t be said, and who gets to control the flow of information.
The result was a highly enjoyable evening.
Thought-provoking questions and new perspectives make Right to Be Forgotten a story of the moment.
Right to Be Forgotten is a compelling story of how life was changed for a young man who did something stupid when he was 17.
Despite losing momentum during its final moments, Right To Be Forgotten is likely to be remembered, especially thanks to the cast’s captivating performances.
This story explores just how powerful the internet can be when it comes to our lives.

cn.t: Critics praise this timely, compelling drama for its gutsy exploration of internet privacy and second chances, with strong performances and sharp direction bringing urgency to questions of forgiveness in the digital age.
